global_issues.title: US-China chip export controls shift to case-by-case licensing
global_issues.note: Confirmed: BIS moved to case-by-case licensing (from presumption of denial) with a 25% Section 232 tariff on advanced semiconductors, effective mid-January 2026, still in force. However, framing this as the primary driver of today's tech selloff is misleading — the dominant driver on 2026-07-29 was a hawkish Fed rate hold plus AI-capex sustainability doubts and Chinese memory/AI-chip competition (CXMT, DeepSeek), not new export-control news.

global_issues.title: Iran Strait of Hormuz shipping risk remains elevated

Overnight (US time July 28-29), Iran launched a ballistic missile attack on US forces (intercepted by CENTCOM), the US and Saudi forces struck Iranian-linked sites in Iraq in retaliation, Iranian Revolutionary Guard forces halted/struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent crude spiked 6.6% to $89.61. Trump publicly vowed further strikes ('they're going to get a beating'). This is a material escalation the briefing missed.

global_issues.title: US DOJ signals renewed AI antitrust scrutiny on big tech
global_issues.note: Consistent with ongoing DOJ/Senate scrutiny of Google-Anthropic and Microsoft-OpenAI partnerships and the broader Google antitrust remedies case extending into GenAI products. No contradicting news found in the last 24h, though this was not a major market mover today relative to the Fed decision and Iran escalation.

grok_report.summary: The briefing's individual global-context items are mostly factually grounded but omit the two dominant market-moving events of the day — the Fed's hawkish rate hold and an overnight Iran-US military escalation that directly contradicts its own Hormuz 'no new incidents' claim. It also mischaracterizes VIX behavior (claims a 13% spike vs. an actual ~2.5% decline) and carries stale earnings dates/prices for META, MSFT, AMZN, and NVDA, including missing that META and MSFT had already reported (with META missing badly) by the time the briefing was generated. Sector-level analysis is reasonably accurate, but the overall narrative causality is skewed and several data points need correction.
